methodology: The site, titled 'Who Funded Genocide', says it is published by 'Archive Genocide' and compiled by an unnamed 'member of our team'; corrections go through a Telegram contact channel. It is an advocacy project that counts 'pro-Israel political money' two ways: (a) a compiled member scorecard 'drawn from lobby-group disclosures' that includes bundled individual giving and is marked 'pending independent FEC verification', and (b) FEC-recomputed figures counting only direct committee-to-candidate contributions (FEC pas2, type 24K), plus independent expenditures (Schedule E) reported separately, for a roster of 44 'pro-Israel lobby committees' (J Street explicitly excluded). Cited sources are FEC bulk data (webk committee summaries 2014-2026, Schedule E 2018-2026, pas2 2014-2026, candidate master, itemized individual contributions indiv22/24/26), with OpenSecrets and Track AIPAC used as external cross-checks and archived candidates.proisraelnetwork.org pages for a sponsorship roster. Headline PAC receipts cover the 2022-2026 cycles ($564,409,098) with a 2014-2026 figure ($712,883,972); the donor database is 'concentrated in calendar 2025, with some records reaching back to late 2021'; FEC snapshots were fetched 2026-11-01 (verification generated 2026-11-01; summary.json build 2026-08-29; home page 'Generated 2026-08-25').

notes: All 44 roster PACs have FEC IDs shown on their own site pages; none needed lookup from tracker FEC data. J Street IDs come from the site's network_pacs.v2.json "excluded" note.
Democratic Majority for Israel (IE) has ID C90022864 (a C9 independent-expenditure filer ID, not C00 format) and shows $0 receipts.

Receipts on the /committee/ index and committee pages are 2014-2026 totals (network_pacs.v2.json); pac_receipts.json gives 2022-2026 totals (sums to $564,409,097.79). Note verification.json says the 2022-2026 file covers "10 core committees" but the file actually lists all 44.

Labels: the site assigns no category beyond "pro-Israel lobby committee" plus an IE-target tag (US House (mixed) / presidential / presidential (mixed)); "AIPAC" and "super PAC" labels here come only from the parenthetical in the name as the site shows it.

fec_tracker_match sums contribution_receipt_amount by contributor_id from each tracker's committee_contribs_2024.json and committee_contribs_2026.json. memo_code "X" rows are earmarked individual contributions itemized with the conduit PAC as contributor_id (memo_text e.g. "EARMARKED THROUGH THIS ORGANIZATION"); direct rows are memo_code null. No duplicate transaction rows found. A name-pattern scan for pro-Israel PAC names without matching IDs found none.

The tracker FEC totals differ from the site's member figures (e.g. Rivas: site FEC direct $17,007 incl. $15,007 AIPAC-linked; tracker data shows $20,000 direct from AIPAC PAC + $4,500 DMFI PAC over 2024 and 2026 cycles). The site does not state the cycle window for member figures; likely different periods/scope.

Site languages (/ar/, /de/ etc.) and /global/<lang>/ translations were not fetched individually (assumed translations of the same pages); /j-soc/ and /manufacturedconsensus/ pages concern Israeli government spending, not FEC PACs.
Not fetched: data/donors.json, data/receipts/, /downloads/ CSVs, and the 524 member pages other than Rivas and Tran. No pages failed to load (all HTTP 200).

11 committee URLs listed in sitemap.xml (american-principles, american-pro-israel-pac, citypac, democratic-majority-for-israel-ie, heartland-pac, joint-action-committee-jacpac, mid-manhattan-pac, natpac-1947, pac-of-cherry-hill-nj, st-louisans-for-better-government, zioness-pac) return the /committee/ index page at the trailing-slash URL; their actual pages load at <url>index.html. site_url records the sitemap URL.
